`rubyfmt -V` and `rubyfmt --version` print a line beginning with `rubyfmt `; `rubyfmt -h` and `rubyfmt --help` print help containing `Usage: rubyfmt`; none of these outputs contains `rubyfmt-main`.
With `--fail-fast`, a syntax-error input exits 1, a missing named input exits 3, and a missing `@file` list exits 3 even without other inputs.
Formatting `a 1,2,3` from stdin and from a named file each emits exactly `a(1, 2, 3)\n` and exits 0.

Flags `-c`/`--check`, `-i`/`--in-place`, `--stdin-filepath`, `--header-opt-in`, `--header-opt-out`, `--include-gitignored`, `--fail-fast`, and `-V`/`--version` keep their names; exit codes 0, 1, 3, and 5 keep their meanings; formatting style and fixture expectations remain identical.
All documented CLI modes, the library formatting entry point, stdin/stdout/in-place operation, check diffs, ignore handling, and header controls remain available with their documented contracts.
The library returns formatted bytes for `a 1,2,3`; invalid Ruby `a 1,2,,` returns a syntax error mapping to exit code 1, a missing input maps to IO exit code 3, and success maps to 0.

With `--header-opt-in`, input `# rubyfmt: true
a 1,2,3
` becomes `# rubyfmt: true
a(1, 2, 3)
`, while input `a 1,2,3` passes through unchanged.
`editor_plugins/` remains byte-for-byte unchanged and no browser/client UI is added as part of the formatter migration.
Adapted harnesses still run the formatter and assert the same behavior, including exact fixture bytes, idempotency, stress-script output equality, CLI exit codes, and stdout/stderr expectations.

Every file under `fixtures/`, including every `_actual.rb` and `_expected.rb` pair, remains byte-for-byte unchanged, and every file under `editor_plugins/` remains unmodified.
`--include-gitignored` formats a file matched by `.gitignore`, and an explicitly named file is formatted even when its name is matched by `.rubyfmtignore`.
With no positional paths and piped stdin `a 1,2,3`, rubyfmt reads stdin and writes `a(1, 2, 3)\n`; when stdin is a terminal, it prints help instead of reading input.
Without `--check` or `--in-place`, formatted bytes for each input are written to stdout and no input file is modified.
`--stdin-filepath ignored.rb` applies .rubyfmtignore/.gitignore to stdin, and combining `--stdin-filepath` with a positional path or `-i` exits nonzero with a conflict error on stderr.
With `--header-opt-out`, input `# rubyfmt: false\na 1,2,3` is emitted unchanged and the process exits 0.
